text:
Dylan Cozens had the kind of week a second-year Senator wants: two goals in an overtime loss, one a one-timer from the slot, then two assists. "It is frustrating not closing out a 5-2 game in the third," he said after one of them, and the frustration is fair: he has 16 points in 25 games, a decent return for a centre at 17:24 a night who throws hits like a checker (60 already).

The finishing is close to normal, six goals on 7.2 expected. What's held his points down is around him: Ottawa has scored 4.9 fewer goals than the chances deserve with him on the ice, and that usually swings back. The five-on-five picture is mixed: 52% of the expected goals with him on, but about four points worse than without him. Evolving-Hockey liked his defense last season, 53rd among forwards in wins above replacement, mostly from even-strength defense. All Three Zones tracking (Corey Sznajder's) says his offense lives in transition, 53% of his shots off the rush. Our range projects 45 to 66 points.
